claims.text: A machine-learning atomic potential trained on a limited ab initio dataset can replace full ab initio molecular-dynamics sampling.
Training data drawn from both solid and liquid phases can yield accurate phase free energies and fusion properties.
The proposed workflow will cost substantially less than explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
Near melting, elemental and binary systems have significant vibrational-entropy contributions.
Near melting, elemental and binary systems have significant anharmonic contributions.
Near melting, elemental and binary systems have significant electron–vibration-coupling contributions.
A minimal ab initio molecular-dynamics dataset at selected solid- and liquid-phase temperatures is sufficient to train the proposed potential.
The trained potential can be used for extensive free-energy sampling.
Reweighting the machine-learning predictions will preserve the integrity of free-energy and entropy estimates.
The trained potential captures local atomic environments in both solid and liquid phases.
The trained potential captures the anharmonic effects of both solid and liquid phases.
Calibration against ab initio energies and forces from both phases ensures the physical fidelity of the machine-learning potential.
The surrogate potential enables faster configurational-space sampling than full ab initio molecular dynamics.
Reweighting corrects residual potential errors sufficiently for free energies, vibrational entropies, and transition properties to closely reproduce full ab initio molecular-dynamics results.
The workflow will provide approximately a tenfold computational speedup relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
For elemental and binary systems, the workflow will have fidelity comparable to TOR-TILD.
The initial applicability domain is elemental and binary metallic systems from just below to slightly above their melting points.
Application far into superheated states or to chemically complex multicomponent systems may require retraining or adjustment.
